subdomain: 2.1 Select appropriate Claude models based on trade-offs

en.question: A strong coordinator currently extracts records from document packets. The proposed optimization delegates independent document extractions to lower-cost worker models and leaves reconciliation to the coordinator. Required fields include visually encoded annotations. Which findings justify admitting a worker model into this design? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Its input-token price is lower, even though failed extractions require repeated worker calls and coordinator repair.
options.note: Unit token price does not capture retries, handoffs, or reconciliation. Lower worker pricing alone can coexist with higher total operating cost.

options.text: Representative packet and reconciliation tests confirm required input support and faithful annotation handoffs.
options.note: The coordinator can only reconcile information that reaches it. Testing the input modality and handoff fidelity addresses capability loss introduced by delegation.

options.text: The coordinator's benchmark remains unchanged when tested without worker-produced inputs.
options.note: That test bypasses the changed part of the design. It cannot detect missing fields or distortions in worker outputs.

options.text: The complete route passes quality and timing gates more cheaply, counting failures and coordinator work.
options.note: Multi-model delegation is justified by the combined system's trade-off. Counting coordination and failure costs avoids attributing component-level savings to the whole workflow.
